Bench: J.K. Maheshwari, Rajesh Bindal
 In The Supreme Court Of India
 Civil Original Jurisdiction
 Transfer Petition (Civil) No. 3223 Of 2023
 Geetika Jolly Petitioner(s)
 Versus
 Dipin Mutreja Respondent(s)
 Order

1) The present petition has been filed by the petitioner(wife) seeking transfer of HMA No. 1971 of 2023 Dipin Mutreja v. Gitika Jolly filed by the respondent (husband) seeking decree of divorce,
pending before the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, North West District, Rohini, Delhi.

sentences.text: 2) As requested and by consent, vide order dated 24.04.2024, the parties were referred to the Supreme Court Mediation Centre to resolve their dispute by way of mediation.
Vide communication dated 09.08.24, the Mediation Centre has forwarded Settlement Agreement dated 08.08.2024 entered between the parties.

The parties have also filed Interlocutory Application No.287005 of 2024 praying decree of divorce by mutual consent as per the settlement arrived at by invoking powers of this Court under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
3) We have interacted with the petitioner(wife) and the respondent(husband), who are present in the Court.
They have been identified by their respective advocates.
During interaction, both have agreed to the terms of the settlement, and prayed for decree of divorce by mutual consent.

4) According to the settlement, the parties have decided to part ways from the matrimonial knot and live separately by mutual consent subject to payment of a sum of 62,50,000/
 by the husband in favour of the wife and the minor child.

The details of the cheques and amount paid are as under:

6) The petitioner has acknowledged the payment of 62,50,000/
 and accepted it as full and final amount for past, present and future claims.

9) In view of the above, considering the settlement agreement and the joint application filed by the parties, we deem it appropriate to dispose of this Transfer Petition with the following directions:
(i) As acknowledged by the petitioner(wife) present in the Court, the amount of 62,50,000/
, as agreed to, has been paid by the respondent(husband) to her as full and final amount and she shall have no claim of any nature whatsoever present, past and future including permanent alimony against the respondent(husband) and his family members.
(ii) The criminal cases, namely, FIR No.559/2022 dated 26.07.2022 PS Civil Lines,
Karnal under Section 323/406/498A/506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, and Complaint No.398/2022 under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, pending in the Court of Illaqua Magistrate, Karnal, be treated as quashed and shall be consigned to the record.
( i i i ) T h e c a s e s o f c i v i l n a t u r e , n a m e l y , ( a ) M a i n t e n a n c e P e t i t i o n No.MNT/125/344/2023 under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 pending in the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, Karnal; (b)HMA No.1971/2023 under Section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, pending in the Court of Principal Judge, Family Court, North West Rohini;
and (c)the Guardianship and Wards case bearing GW No.33/2024 pending before Additional Principal Judge, Family Court, Karnal, be treated as disposed of and shall be consigned to the records.
(iv) Accepting the terms of the settlement and as consented by the parties, on their request in exercise of our jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution, we grant the decree of divorce by mutual consent.
